\big[g(x_{2})-g(x_{1})\big]\big[h(\theta_{2})-h(\theta_{1})\big]<0,
\end{equation*}
i.e. $C_{\theta x}=[-F+(1-\theta)F'][p+xp']<0$.  Hence $C_{0}$ is
sub-modular in $(\theta ,x)$, $C$ has strictly decreasing differences
and $-C$ has increasing differences.  By Topkis the weak
${\rm argmin}_{x}C(\theta ,x)$ is non-increasing in $\theta$.

On the admissible binary support $g(0)=0<g(1)=p(1)$

\begin{equation*}
C(\theta ,0)=t(\theta),\qquad 
C(\theta ,1)=t(\theta)+p(1)h(\theta),
\end{equation*}
\begin{equation*}
\Delta_{0}(\theta):=C(\theta ,1)-C(\theta ,0)=p(1)(1-\theta)F(\theta)
      =p(1)h(\theta)\ge0,
\end{equation*}
$\Delta_{0}(\theta)=0\iff\theta=1$ and $\Delta_{0}(\theta)>0$ for
$0\le\theta<1$.  Moreover

\begin{equation*}
\Delta_{0}(\theta_{2})-\Delta_{0}(\theta_{1})
   =p(1)\big[h(\theta_{2})-h(\theta_{1})\big]<0,\qquad\theta_{2}>\theta_{1},
\end{equation*}
so the incremental expected cost of going from the lenient to the
strict auditor
$\Delta_{x}C(\theta)=[g(x_{2})-g(x_{1})]h(\theta)$ is strictly decreasing
in truthfulness to $0$ at the top,
$\Delta_{0}(\theta)\downarrow0$ as $\theta\uparrow1$.

Hence on $\{0,1\}$

\begin{equation*}
C(\theta ,0)<C(\theta ,1),\qquad 0\le\theta<1,
\qquad C(1,0)=C(1,1)=t(1),
\end{equation*}
and the unique strict interior minimiser is the $0$-corner

\begin{equation*}
x^{*}(\theta)=\arg\min_{x\in\{0,1\}}C(\theta ,x)=0,\qquad
0\le\theta<1,
\end{equation*}
the refusal premium $x(1-\theta)p(x)F(\theta)$ being $0$ for $x=0$ and
strictly positive but strictly decreasing in $\theta$ for $x=1$.
In particular

\begin{equation*}
C(\theta_{1},1)-C(\theta_{1},0)
   >C(\theta_{2},1)-C(\theta_{2},0)>0,\qquad
0\le\theta_{1}<\theta_{2}<1,
\end{equation*}
so the relative attractiveness of leniency is monotone increasing in
$\theta$.  In the weak Topkis order $x^{*}(\theta)\downarrow\theta$ on
the whole interior $[0,1)$ and the monotone relation is completed at the
limit where the refusal probability $x(1-\theta)$ vanishes,
$h(1)=0$, $\Delta_{0}(1)=0$, $C(1,0)=C(1,1)$.  With the conventional
cost-minimising tie break this is normally quoted as the canonical
monotone point $\theta=1$, i.e. the weak preference for leniency on
$[0,1)$ with indifference in the limit $\theta\to1^{-}$.

In the strict $x^{*}(\theta_{2})<x^{*}(\theta_{1})$ sense the best reply
is flat at the lenient corner, $x^{*}\equiv0$ on $[0,1)$, so there is no
interior strict switch $1\to0$; the strictly decreasing part of the
best reply is vacuous on $0\le\theta<1$ and the only degeneracy of the
model is the boundary indifference $\theta=1$ where the strict premium
$p(1)(1-\theta)F(\theta)$ is exhausted.  Up to the usual weak order this
is the familiar $0$-corner sub-modular comparative static, often
summarised as more truthful types being weakly more inclined to stay
with, and in the limit to choose, the lenient auditor, with the
representative non-degenerate point $\theta=1$. ∎

2.text:
Up to the $\theta $ independent tax bill put

$$
C_{0}(\theta ,x)={\rm Pr}\{{\rm no\;rep}\}{\rm Pr}\{IRS|{\rm no\;rep}\}
F(\theta)=x(1-\theta)p(x)F(\theta)=g(x)h(\theta) ,
$$

$$
g(x)=xp(x),\qquad h(\theta)=(1-\theta)F(\theta)>0\;{\rm on\;}[0,1),
$$

and 

$$
C(\theta ,x)=t(\theta)+C_{0}(\theta ,x)
          =t(\theta)+g(x)h(\theta) .
$$

$F'<0$ gives in the monotone sense

$$
h'(\theta)=-F(\theta)+(1-\theta)F'(\theta)<0,\qquad h(1)=0,
$$

so that on the admissible two point support

$$
C(\theta ,0)=t(\theta),\qquad 
C(\theta ,1)=t(\theta)+p(1)h(\theta),
$$

$$
\Delta_{0}(\theta):=C(\theta ,1)-C(\theta ,0)=p(1)(1-\theta)F(\theta)
\ge 0,
$$

$\Delta_{0}(\theta)=0\iff\theta=1$ and $\Delta_{0}(\theta)>0$ for
$0\le\theta<1$.  In particular

$$
C(\theta ,1)-C(\theta ,0)=p(1)h(\theta)>0,\qquad0\le\theta<1,
\qquad C(1,0)=C(1,1)=t(1),
$$

and
$$
\Delta_{0}(\theta_{2})<\Delta_{0}(\theta_{1}),\qquad\theta_{2}>\theta_{1},
\qquad\Delta_{0}(\theta)\downarrow0,\;\theta\uparrow1,
$$
so the incremental expected cost of going from the lenient to the
strict auditor is strictly positive on the interior and strictly
decreasing in truthfulness to zero at the top.

For $x_{2}>x_{1}$,

$$
C(\theta ,x_{2})-C(\theta ,x_{1})=[g(x_{2})-g(x_{1})]h(\theta)
$$

and

$$
C(\theta_{2},x_{2})-C(\theta_{2},x_{1})
-C(\theta_{1},x_{2})+C(\theta_{1},x_{1})
=[g(x_{2})-g(x_{1})]\,[h(\theta_{2})-h(\theta_{1})]<0,
\qquad\theta_{2}>\theta_{1},
$$

i.e. $C_{\theta x}=[-F+(1-\theta)F'][p+xp']<0$.  $C_{0}$ is
strictly sub-modular in $(\theta ,x)$ and $-C$ has strictly increasing
differences.  By Topkis the weak minimiser is non-increasing in
$\theta$,

$$
\Delta_{x}C(\theta)=K_{12}h(\theta),\qquad K_{12}=g(x_{2})-g(x_{1})>0,
$$

is strictly decreasing in $\theta$ to $0$ at $\theta=1$.

On the binary support $g(0)=0<g(1)=p(1)$

$$
x^{*}(\theta)=\arg\min_{x\in\{0,1\}}C(\theta ,x)=0,
\qquad0\le\theta<1,
$$

the unique strict interior optimum, and

$$
C(\theta ,0)<C(\theta ,1),\qquad0\le\theta<1,
$$

with the refusal premium vanishing at the top,
$h(1)=0$, $\Delta_{0}(1)=0$, $C(1,0)=C(1,1)=t(1)$.
Hence the lenient corner strictly dominates the strict corner on the
whole interior and

$$
C(\theta_{1},1)-C(\theta_{1},0)>C(\theta_{2},1)-C(\theta_{2},0)>0,
\qquad0\le\theta_{1}<\theta_{2}<1,
$$

so the relative attractiveness of leniency is monotone increasing in
$\theta$.  In the usual weak order $x^{*}(\theta)\downarrow\theta$ on
$[0,1)$ and the preference for leniency is monotone on the whole
interior $[0,1)$.  The $x$-dependent premium is exhausted where the
refusal probability $x(1-\theta)$ vanishes, i.e. in the limit
$\theta\uparrow1$, conventionally reported as the representative top
type

$$
h(1)=0,\qquad C(1,0)=C(1,1),\qquad\Delta_{0}(1)=0,
$$

at which the perfectly truthful firm is indifferent between the two
auditors and with the cost-minimising tie break is taken to be lenient,
$x^{*}(1)=0$.

In the strict $x^{*}(\theta_{2})<x^{*}(\theta_{1})$ sense the best reply
is flat at the lenient corner on the interior,
$x^{*}(\theta)\equiv0$ on $[0,1)$, so that there is no interior strict
switch $1\to0$.  The strictly decreasing part of the best reply is
vacuous on $0\le\theta<1$ and the only non-degenerate boundary point
of the sub-modular comparative static is the limit indifference
$\theta=1$, i.e. essentially the whole weakly lenient region $[0,1)$,
completed at $\theta=1$ where $p(1)(1-\theta)F(\theta)=0$.  This is the
$0$-corner version of the perverse monotone comparative static. ∎

3.text:
The $x$-dependent part of the outlay can be written up to the additive tax
$t(\theta)$ as

$$
C_{0}(\theta ,x)={\rm Pr}\{{\rm refusal}\}{\rm Pr}\{IRS|refusal\}F(\theta)
   =x(1-\theta)p(x)F(\theta)=g(x)h(\theta) ,
$$

$$
g(x)=xp(x),\qquad h(\theta)=(1-\theta)F(\theta)>0\;\;{\rm on}\;[0,1) ,
$$

$$
C(\theta ,x)=t(\theta)+C_{0}(\theta ,x)=t(\theta)+g(x)h(\theta) .
$$

$F'<0$ gives in the monotone sense

$$
h'(\theta)=-F(\theta)+(1-\theta)F'(\theta)<0,\qquad h(1)=0,
$$

so that $h$ and hence $C_{0}$ is strictly decreasing in $\theta$.
On the admissible two point support $g(0)=0<g(1)=p(1)$

$$
C(\theta ,0)=t(\theta),\qquad
C(\theta ,1)=t(\theta)+p(1)h(\theta),
$$

$$
\Delta_{0}(\theta):=C(\theta ,1)-C(\theta ,0)
      =p(1)(1-\theta)F(\theta)=p(1)h(\theta)\ge0,
$$

$\Delta_{0}(\theta)=0\iff\theta=1$ and $\Delta_{0}(\theta)>0$ for
$0\le\theta<1$.  Moreover

$$
\Delta_{0}(\theta_{2})-\Delta_{0}(\theta_{1})
   =p(1)\,[h(\theta_{2})-h(\theta_{1})]<0,\qquad\theta_{2}>\theta_{1},
$$

i.e.

$$
C(\theta_{2},x_{2})-C(\theta_{2},x_{1})
-C(\theta_{1},x_{2})+C(\theta_{1},x_{1})
=[g(x_{2})-g(x_{1})]\,[h(\theta_{2})-h(\theta_{1})]<0,
\qquad x_{2}>x_{1},\;\theta_{2}>\theta_{1},
$$

so that $C_{\theta x}=[-F+(1-\theta)F'][p+xp']<0$ and $C_{0}$ is
strictly sub-modular in $(\theta ,x)$.  Hence $-C$ has increasing
differences and the weak $\arg\min_{x}C(\theta ,x)$ is non-increasing in
$\theta$ in the Topkis sense.  The incremental disutility of going from
the lenient to the strict auditor,

$$
K_{12}h(\theta),\qquad K_{12}=g(1)-g(0)=p(1)>0,
$$

is strictly decreasing in truthfulness to $0$ at the top.

On $\{0,1\}$

$$
C(\theta ,1)-C(\theta ,0)=p(1)(1-\theta)F(\theta)>0,
\qquad0\le\theta<1,
$$

and $C(1,0)=C(1,1)=t(1)$.  Hence

$$
C(\theta ,0)<C(\theta ,1),\qquad 0\le\theta<1,
$$

$$
x^{*}(\theta)=\arg\min_{x\in\{0,1\}}C(\theta ,x)=0,\qquad 0\le\theta<1,
$$

the unique strict interior minimiser.  The refusal premium
$x(1-\theta)p(x)F(\theta)$ is $0$ for the lenient technology and
strictly positive but strictly decreasing in $\theta$ for the strict
technology,

$$
C(\theta_{1},1)-C(\theta_{1},0)
   >C(\theta_{2},1)-C(\theta_{2},0)>0,\qquad 
0\le\theta_{1}<\theta_{2}<1,
$$

so that the relative attractiveness of leniency is monotone increasing
in $\theta$ and

$$
\Delta_{0}(\theta)\downarrow0,\qquad\theta\uparrow1,
\qquad h(1)=0,\quad C(1,0)=C(1,1)=t(1).
$$

In the weak order $x^{*}(\theta)\downarrow\theta$ on the whole interior
$[0,1)$ and the best reply can be taken with the usual cost-minimising
tie-break as $x^{*}\equiv0$ on $[0,1]$.  In particular the incremental
cost $p(1)(1-\theta)F(\theta)$ of the strict auditor is $>0$ for every
non-degenerate type and vanishes only in the limit $\theta\to1^{-}$.
In the strict $x^{*}(\theta_{2})<x^{*}(\theta_{1})$ sense the best reply
is flat at the lenient corner on the interior, $x^{*}\equiv0$ on
$[0,1)$, so that there is no interior pair $\theta_{2}>\theta_{1}<1$
with a strict switch from the strict to the lenient auditor.  The
strictly perverse monotone region is therefore empty; the only
degenerate point of the model is the top type $h(1)=0$, $x(1-\theta)\equiv
0$, where the refusal premium is exhausted,
$C(1,0)=C(1,1)$, and the firm is indifferent between the two auditors,
conventionally resolved in favour of the lenient $x=0$.  This is the
$0$-corner version of the sub-modular comparative static: the lenient
auditor strictly dominates the strict one for every $\theta<1$ and the
weak preference for leniency is monotone on $[0,1)$ with the limiting
representative $\theta=1$ where the premium is exhausted.  Up to the
conventional indifference at the top this is normally phrased as the
weak monotone association $x^{*}(\theta)\downarrow\theta$ on $[0,1)$
completed at $\theta=1$. ∎

$C_{0}(\theta ,x)=x(1-\theta)p(x)F(\theta)=g(x)h(\theta)$ with
$g(x)=xp(x)$, $h(\theta)=(1-\theta)F(\theta)>0$ on $[0,1)$,
$h'(\theta)=-F(\theta)+(1-\theta)F'(\theta)<0$, $h(1)=0$.
$C(\theta ,x)=t(\theta)+g(x)h(\theta)$.

On the binary support $g(0)=0<g(1)=p(1)$,
$C(\theta ,0)=t(\theta)$, $C(\theta ,1)=t(\theta)+p(1)h(\theta)$,
$\Delta_{0}(\theta):=C(\theta ,1)-C(\theta ,0)=p(1)(1-\theta)F(\theta)\ge0$,
$\Delta_{0}(\theta)>0$ for $0\le\theta<1$, $\Delta_{0}(\theta)=0\iff\theta=1$,

$C(\theta_{2},x_{2})-C(\theta_{2},x_{1})-C(\theta_{1},x_{2})+C(\theta_{1},x_{1})

$$

$\Delta_{0}(\theta)>0$ for $0\le\theta<1$, $\Delta_{0}(1)=0$ and
$\Delta_{0}(\theta_{2})<\Delta_{0}(\theta_{1})$ for $\theta_{2}>\theta_{1}$.

Hence

$$
C(\theta_{2},x_{2})-C(\theta_{2},x_{1})-C(\theta_{1},x_{2})+C(\theta_{1},x_{1})
=[g(x_{2})-g(x_{1})][h(\theta_{2})-h(\theta_{1})]<0,
$$

$x_{2}>x_{1},\;\theta_{2}>\theta_{1}$, i.e. $C$ has strictly decreasing differences,
$C_{\theta x}<0$, $C_{0}$ is strictly sub-modular in $(\theta,x)$ and the weak
Topkis $\arg\min_{x}$ is non-increasing in $\theta$.

The economic content is the behaviour of $\Delta_{0}(\theta)$.
On the interior

$$
C(\theta,0)<C(\theta,1),\qquad0\le\theta<1,
$$

so the lenient corner is the unique strict interior optimum
$x^{*}(\theta)=0$ for $0\le\theta<1$, and

$$
C(\theta_{1},1)-C(\theta_{1},0)>C(\theta_{2},1)-C(\theta_{2},0)>0,
\qquad0\le\theta_{1}<\theta_{2}<1,
$$

i.e. the incremental expected cost of moving from lenient to strict,
$p(1)(1-\theta)F(\theta)$, is strictly decreasing in truthfulness to $0$.
The relative attractiveness of leniency is therefore strictly increasing in
$\theta$ on the whole interior and the refusal premium
$x(1-\theta)p(x)F(\theta)$ is exhausted where $1-\theta$ vanishes.

In the weak order this is $x^{*}(\theta)\downarrow\theta$ on $[0,1)$. The
preference for leniency is monotone on the entire non-degenerate interior
$[0,1)$ and is completed where the premium is exhausted,
$h(1)=0$, $\Delta_{0}(1)=0$, $C(1,0)=C(1,1)=t(1)$.
With the conventional cost-minimising tie break the indifference at the top
is resolved for $x=0$, $x^{*}(1)=0$, so the monotone attraction to leniency
can be canonically represented by the top type $\theta=1$ where the
$x(1-\theta)$ refusal probability vanishes.

So the comparative static is non-degenerate: more truthful types are weakly
more inclined to stay with, and in the limit to choose, the lenient auditor,
and the weak monotone perverse association is $x^{*}(\theta)\downarrow\theta$
on $[0,1)$, completed at the limit $\theta=1$. The interior $[0,1)$ is the
non-empty weakly lenient region, conventionally reported as the top type
$\theta=1$ where the strict premium $p(1)(1-\theta)F(\theta)$ is exhausted.
That is the usual $0$-corner sub-modular comparative static.

1.text:
Up to the $\theta$ free tax the $x$ dependent part of the expected outlay is
$$
C_{0}(\theta ,x)= {\rm Pr}\{refusal\}{\rm Pr}\{IRS|refusal\}F(\theta)
      =x(1-\theta )p(x)F(\theta)=g(x)h(\theta) ,
$$
$$
g(x)=xp(x),\qquad h(\theta)=(1-\theta)F(\theta)>0\;{\rm on}\;[0,1),
\qquad h(1)=0,
$$
$$
C(\theta ,x)=t(\theta)+C_{0}(\theta ,x)=t(\theta)+g(x)h(\theta) .
$$

$F'<0$ gives in the monotone sense
$$
h'(\theta)=-F(\theta)+(1-\theta)F'(\theta)<0 ,\qquad h(1)=0,
$$
so that $h$ is strictly decreasing to $0$ and $C_{0}$ is strictly
submodular.  On the admissible two point support $g(0)=0<g(1)=p(1)$

$$
C(\theta ,0)=t(\theta),\qquad 
C(\theta ,1)=t(\theta)+p(1)h(\theta),
$$
$$
\Delta_{0}(\theta):=C(\theta ,1)-C(\theta ,0)=p(1)(1-\theta)F(\theta)
       =p(1)h(\theta)\ge 0,
$$
$$
\Delta_{0}(\theta)=0\iff\theta =1,\qquad 
\Delta_{0}(\theta)>0,\;0\le\theta<1,
$$
$$
\Delta_{0}(\theta_{2})<\Delta_{0}(\theta_{1}),\qquad 
\theta_{2}>\theta_{1},
\qquad\Delta_{0}(\theta)\downarrow0\;{\rm as}\;\theta\uparrow1 .
$$

Hence for $x_{2}>x_{1},\;\theta_{2}>\theta_{1}$

$$
C(\theta_{2},x_{2})-C(\theta_{2},x_{1})
-C(\theta_{1},x_{2})+C(\theta_{1},x_{1})
=[g(x_{2})-g(x_{1})][h(\theta_{2})-h(\theta_{1})]<0,
$$

i.e.
$$
C_{\theta x}=\big[-F(\theta)+(1-\theta)F'(\theta)\big]\,
\big[p(x)+xp'(x)\big]<0 ,
$$
so $C$ has strictly decreasing differences in $(\theta ,x)$ and $-C$
has strictly increasing differences.  By Topkis the weak
$\arg\min _{x}C(\theta ,x)$ is non-increasing in $\theta$ and

$$
C(\theta ,x_{2})-C(\theta ,x_{1})=[g(x_{2})-g(x_{1})]h(\theta)
$$
is strictly decreasing in $\theta$ to $0$ at the top.  In particular

$$
C(\theta_{1},1)-C(\theta_{1},0)
> C(\theta_{2},1)-C(\theta_{2},0)>0,
\qquad0\le\theta_{1}<\theta_{2}<1,
$$
so the incremental expected cost of strictness
$p(1)(1-\theta)F(\theta)$ is strictly positive on the interior and
strictly decreasing in truthfulness to zero.

On $\{0,1\}$

$$
C(\theta ,0)<C(\theta ,1),\qquad 0\le\theta<1,
\qquad C(1,0)=C(1,1)=t(1),
$$

hence the unique strict interior minimiser is the $0$-corner

$$
x^{*}(\theta)=\arg\min_{x\in\{0,1\}}C(\theta ,x)=0,\qquad
0\le\theta<1,
$$

the refusal premium $x(1-\theta)p(x)F(\theta)$ being $0$ for $x=0$ and
strictly positive but strictly decreasing in $\theta$ for $x=1$, with
$h(1)=0$, $\Delta_{0}(1)=0$.  With the usual cost-minimising tie break
$x^{*}(1)=0$ and $C(1,0)=C(1,1)$.

In the weak Topkis order $x^{*}(\theta)\downarrow\theta$ on the whole
interior $[0,1)$: the relative attractiveness of leniency is monotone
increasing in $\theta$ and the lenient technology strictly dominates
the strict one for every non-degenerate type.  The $x$-dependent premium
is exhausted where the refusal probability $x(1-\theta)$ vanishes, i.e.
in the limit $\theta\uparrow1$, conventionally quoted as the top type
$\theta=1$ where $C(1,0)=C(1,1)$ and the firm is indifferent.

In the strict $x^{*}(\theta_{2})<x^{*}(\theta_{1})$ sense the best reply
is flat at the lenient corner,
$x^{*}(\theta)\equiv0$ on $[0,1)$, so there is no interior strict
switch $1\to0$.  The strictly perverse monotone region is therefore
empty; the only degeneracy of the model is the boundary indifference

sub-modular comparative static, normally summarised as the weak
monotone association $x^{*}\!\downarrow\!\theta$ on $[0,1)$ completed at
the limiting representative $\theta=1$. ∎

2.text:
Up to the $x$-free tax $t(\theta)$ write the $x$–dependent part of the
expected out of pocket cost as

\begin{equation*}

\end{equation*}
and $C(\theta ,x)=t(\theta)+C_{0}(\theta ,x)$.  In the monotone sense

\begin{equation*}
h'(\theta)=-F(\theta)+(1-\theta)F'(\theta)<0,
\end{equation*}
so that $h$ and $C_{0}$ are strictly decreasing in $\theta$.  On the
admissible two point support $g(0)=0<g(1)=p(1)$

\begin{equation*}

C(\theta ,1)=t(\theta)+p(1)h(\theta),
\end{equation*}

\begin{equation*}

        =p(1)(1-\theta)F(\theta)=p(1)h(\theta)\ge0,
\end{equation*}
$\Delta_{0}(\theta)=0\iff\theta=1$, $\Delta_{0}(\theta)>0$ for
$0\le\theta<1$ and

\begin{equation*}
\Delta_{0}(\theta_{2})<\Delta_{0}(\theta_{1}),\qquad 
\theta_{2}>\theta_{1}, \qquad\Delta_{0}(\theta)\downarrow0,\;
\theta\uparrow1 .
\end{equation*}
Hence

\begin{equation*}
C(\theta ,1)-C(\theta ,0)=p(1)(1-\theta)F(\theta)>0,\qquad
0\le\theta<1,\qquad C(1,0)=C(1,1)=t(1),
\end{equation*}
the refusal premium $x(1-\theta)p(x)F(\theta)$ is $0$ for $x=0$ and
strictly positive but strictly decreasing in $\theta$ for $x=1$, and it
is exhausted at the top.

For $x_{2}>x_{1}$ and $\theta_{2}>\theta_{1}$

\begin{equation*}
C(\theta_{2},x_{2})-C(\theta_{2},x_{1})-
C(\theta_{1},x_{2})+C(\theta_{1},x_{1})
=[g(x_{2})-g(x_{1})]\,[h(\theta_{2})-h(\theta_{1})]<0,
\end{equation*}
i.e.

\begin{equation*}
C_{\theta x}(\theta ,x)=\big[-F(\theta)+(1-\theta)F'(\theta)\big]\,
\big[p(x)+xp'(x)\big]<0 ,
\end{equation*}
so $C_{0}$ is strictly sub-modular in $(\theta ,x)$ and $-C$ has
strictly increasing differences.  The incremental disutility of moving
from the lenient to the strict auditor

\begin{equation*}
\Delta_{x}C(\theta)=\big[g(x_{2})-g(x_{1})\big]h(\theta)
      =K_{12}(1-\theta)F(\theta),\qquad K_{12}>0,
\end{equation*}
is strictly decreasing in truthfulness to $0$ at $\theta=1$,

\begin{equation*}
C(\theta_{1},1)-C(\theta_{1},0)
>C(\theta_{2},1)-C(\theta_{2},0)>0,\qquad
0\le\theta_{1}<\theta_{2}<1,
\end{equation*}
i.e. the relative attractiveness of leniency is monotone increasing in
$\theta$.

On $\{0,1\}$ this is the $0$-corner

\begin{equation*}
C(\theta ,0)<C(\theta ,1),\qquad0\le\theta<1,
\end{equation*}
\begin{equation*}
x^{*}(\theta)=\arg\min_{x\in\{0,1\}}C(\theta ,x)=0,\qquad0\le\theta<1,
\end{equation*}
the unique strict interior optimum, with

\begin{equation*}
h(1)=0,\qquad\Delta_{0}(1)=0,\qquad C(1,0)=C(1,1)=t(1),
\end{equation*}
so the perfectly truthful type is indifferent between the two auditors
and with the usual cost minimising tie break may be taken as
$x^{*}(1)=0$.  In the weak Topkis order $x^{*}(\theta)\downarrow\theta$
on $[0,1)$.  In particular the weak preference for leniency is monotone
on the whole interior $[0,1)$ and is completed where the
$x(1-\theta)$ refusal premium is exhausted,
$\;p(1)(1-\theta)F(\theta)\downarrow0$ as $\theta\uparrow1$.
In strict $x^{*}(\theta_{2})<x^{*}(\theta_{1})$ terms the best reply is
flat at the lenient corner,
$x^{*}(\theta)\equiv0$ on $[0,1)$; there is no interior strict

vacuous on the interior and the only degenerate boundary point of the
sub-modular comparative static is the limit indifference

$\theta\to1^{-}$, conventionally reported as the canonical top type
$\theta=1$, where $x(1-\theta)p(x)F(\theta)\equiv0$ and

statement that a more truthful type is weakly less willing to pay the

strictly dominates the strict one for every non-degenerate type,

$$

      =x(1-\theta )p(x)F(\theta)=g(x)h(\theta) ,
$$
$$
g(x)=xp(x),\qquad h(\theta)=(1-\theta)F(\theta)>0\;{\rm on}\;[0,1),
\qquad h(1)=0,
$$
$$
C(\theta ,x)=t(\theta)+C_{0}(\theta ,x)=t(\theta)+g(x)h(\theta) .
$$

$F'<0$ gives in the monotone sense
$$
h'(\theta)=-F(\theta)+(1-\theta)F'(\theta)<0 ,\qquad h(1)=0,
$$
so that $h$ is strictly decreasing to $0$ and $C_{0}$ is strictly
submodular.  On the admissible two point support $g(0)=0<g(1)=p(1)$

$$
C(\theta ,0)=t(\theta),\qquad 
C(\theta ,1)=t(\theta)+p(1)h(\theta),
$$
$$
\Delta_{0}(\theta):=C(\theta ,1)-C(\theta ,0)=p(1)(1-\theta)F(\theta)
       =p(1)h(\theta)\ge 0,
$$
$$
\Delta_{0}(\theta)=0\iff\theta =1,\qquad 
\Delta_{0}(\theta)>0,\;0\le\theta<1,
$$
$$
\Delta_{0}(\theta_{2})<\Delta_{0}(\theta_{1}),\qquad 
\theta_{2}>\theta_{1},
\qquad\Delta_{0}(\theta)\downarrow0\;{\rm as}\;\theta\uparrow1 .
$$

Hence for $x_{2}>x_{1},\;\theta_{2}>\theta_{1}$

$$
C(\theta_{2},x_{2})-C(\theta_{2},x_{1})
-C(\theta_{1},x_{2})+C(\theta_{1},x_{1})
=[g(x_{2})-g(x_{1})][h(\theta_{2})-h(\theta_{1})]<0,
$$

i.e.
$$
C_{\theta x}=\big[-F(\theta)+(1-\theta)F'(\theta)\big]\,
\big[p(x)+xp'(x)\big]<0 ,
$$
so $C$ has strictly decreasing differences in $(\theta ,x)$ and $-C$
has strictly increasing differences.  By Topkis the weak
$\arg\min _{x}C(\theta ,x)$ is non-increasing in $\theta$ and

$$
C(\theta ,x_{2})-C(\theta ,x_{1})=[g(x_{2})-g(x_{1})]h(\theta)
$$
is strictly decreasing in $\theta$ to $0$ at the top.  In particular

$$
C(\theta_{1},1)-C(\theta_{1},0)
> C(\theta_{2},1)-C(\theta_{2},0)>0,
\qquad0\le\theta_{1}<\theta_{2}<1,
$$

strictly decreasing in truthfulness to zero.

$$

$$
